summary: - _(e) Pass such other order(s) and grant relief(s) that this Hon’ble Commission deems fit in the interest of justice and equity._ - _(a) Issue ad-interim injunction upon the Respondent No. 1 from raising monthly GNA Bills on the Petitioner and direct the Respondent No. 1 to refrain from raising monthly GNA Bills._ - _(d) Pass any other or further orders as this Hon'ble Commission may deem fit and in the interest of justice._ - _(b) Issue ad-interim injunction upon the Respondent No. 1 from raising monthly GNA Bills on the Petitioner and direct the Respondent No. 1 to refrain from raising monthly GNA Bills._ - _(c) Direct the Respondent No. 1 to refund to the Petitioner an amount of Rs. 1 Crore paid as one-time GNA charges._ - _(e) Pass any other or further orders as this Hon'ble Commission may deem fit and in the interest of justice_ - l) Being aggrieved by the letter dated 22.08.2024 of the CTUIL, the Petitioner craves leave to file this present petition, inter alia, on the following grounds which are independent of each other: 3. Petition was admitted on 30.09.2024. The relevant extract of the RoP of hearing dated 30.09.2024 is as under: _(a) The Petitioner is a deemed distribution licensee supplying power in the Asansol-Raniganj area of West Bengal._ _(c) Thereafter, for the purpose of constructing the Maithon (ISTS)-Debipur 220 kV line, the Petitioner applied for prior approval of the Central Government under Section 68 of the Electricity Act, 2003 which was denied by the CEA on 14.12.2018 on the ground of jurisdiction. The Petitioner was, therefore, constrained to approach the Hon’ble High Court of Delhi in WP No. 6450/2019 on the issue of who shall be the “Appropriate Government” to issue Section 68 Approval in the case of the Petitioner._ _(f) Pertinently, the WP No. 6450/2019 filed by the Petitioner before the Hon’ble High Court of Delhi was decided only on 30.4.2024, wherein the Hon’ble High Court directed the CEA/ Ministry of Power, Government of India, to consider the Petitioner’s application for Prior Approval under Section 68 of the Act._ _(d) In the Petition, the Petitioner has also sought to invoke the inherent powers of this Commission for allowing its prayers. However, as already held by the Hon’ble Supreme Court, the inherent power of the Commission is available to it for exercise only in those areas where the Act or Rules are silent. In the present case, the GNA Regulations specifically exclude the deferment of the effective date of the GNA on the grounds alleged by the Petitioner. In this regard, the reliance was placed on the judgment of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in the case of Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam Limited v. Solar Semiconductor Power Co. (India) Pvt. Ltd. and Anr., [(2017) 16 SCC 498]._ _5. Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the Petitioner and the Respondent, CTUIL, the Commission ordered as under:_ _(b) The Respondents to file their respective replies within three weeks with a copy to the Petitioner, who may file its rejoinder within three weeks thereafter._ - o) The Petitioner's assertion that the planning for the commissioning of the Maithon sub-station has not been specifically intended for the Petitioner and consequently, there is no loss of transmission charges for CTUIL during the interim period until the Petitioner implements the actual connectivity, and that no issue of stranded capacity arises, is flawed. This is so because the GNA granted to the Petitioner is in a meshed network of the ISTS, wherein, when access has been granted to the Petitioner for a specified quantum, that capacity has become blocked for the Petitioner, thereby precluding its availability for any other entity that may be next in line in seeking access. As such, the liability to pay charges for the same in accordance with the Regulations is necessarily ensured. 8. Petitioner vide affidavit dated 12.12.2024 has filed Rejoinder to reply filed by Respondent CTUIL and has mainly submitted as under: - d) The Petitioner is therefore similarly placed as the “Connectivity grantees covered under Regulation 4.1”. It is settled law that similarly placed cannot be dissimilarly treated so as to make such a treatment violative of Article 14 of the Constitution of India. - f) The Petitioner has sought remedy and relief under the present petition since the CTUIL i.e. the “Nodal Agency” has failed to “review and take corrective action” under Regulation 11.3 of the GNA Regulations based on _the status of implementation of work under the scope of the connectivity grantee and status of implementation of the ATS and terminal bay(s) as updated._ - g) The Petitioner in the present Petition has sought remedy and relief under the above provisions as well as Regulation 41 (Power to Relax) of the GNA Regulations. relinquishment charges will be applicable or waived if the Petitioner accedes to these submissions/ suggestions of CTUIL. 10. Considering their request, the Commission permitted both sides to file their respective written submissions, if any, within 4 days, with a copy to the other side. 13. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner, Respondent and perused the facts available on the record. 20. We have considered the submission of the Petitioner and Respondent. The following issues arise for our consideration: Delhi High Court Order dated 30.04.2024, and the MoP Sec-68 approval vide letter dated 18.06.2024 is as under. _23. For the aforesaid reasons, I hold that the Petitioner’s application under Section 68 of the Act was liable to be considered by the Central Government, as the “appropriate government” under Section 2(5)(a)(ii) of the Act._ _24. In view of the above, the petition is allowed, The impugned order dated 14.12.2018 is set aside, and the petitioner’s request for approval under Section 68 of the Act is remanded to CEA for expeditious consideration and disposal. .”_
